A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CDTD research work, with 40 readable pages and matching main text, references, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-U. No material reading gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original CDTD benchmark experiments and ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1-2, supplemented by sensitivity analyses, dataset-level results and runtime measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 2-3 and Appendices K-L retain the same score matching/interpolation framework, loss calibration, adaptive noise schedules, architecture and deterministic sampling algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eleven datasets listed in Appendix F/Table 3, with identical regression and binary-classification tasks. Supplementary experimental scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SMOTE, ARF, CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, CoDi and TabSyn, with identical dataset-specific exclusions. The separate CDTD-versus-TabSyn comparison in Appendix N is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both specify the same 60/20/20 splits, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, sample limits, model configurations, training budgets and model-specific sampling steps (Section 4; Appendices H-L).

E4.justification: The five-configuration ablation, sampling-step and hyperparameter sensitivity tests, latent-space comparison, learned-schedule analyses and qualitative correlation comparisons are unchanged (Table 2; Appendices A, L-N, P-R and T).

E5.justification: Both retain five sampling seeds and ten downstream-model seeds for machine learning efficiency. Standard-error and standard-deviation reporting in the appendix tables is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, qualitative findings and runtime measurements match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains CDTD (per type)'s average RMSE rank of 2.6 and detection-score rank of 1.6 in both versions.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Assumption 1 and Proposition 1 in Section 3.2 are identical. The loss-calibration proof, initialization derivations, noise-schedule mathematics and sampling derivation in the appendices are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning unified continuous diffusion, data-type homogenization, sample quality, scalability and compatibility with advanced diffusion techniques.

C2.justification: Interpretations of noise-schedule and latent-diffusion results are unchanged. The same limitations concerning hyperparameter tuning, privacy, specialized data and imputation remain in Section 5.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, software versions, hardware and training information in Appendices G-L are identical. The replication-code disclosure and code-access links are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list, introduction's prior-work discussion and research positioning in Appendices N-O are unchanged. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v5 dated 8 April 2025 to v6 dated 15 January 2026. This is an administrative text update; the paper's prose, headings, terminology and organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-25, Tables 1-29 and Algorithm 1 retain the same visual content, structure, captions and placement. The updated version/date text does not change the document layout.

improvement.justification: The complete main text and Appendices A-U retain the same methods, mathematical arguments, experiments, results and discussion. The administrative version/date update provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in scientific support, clarity or reproducibility.
